title: Preemptive soft-fallback controller and decision telemetry for region/tier routing
creator: Aisha Malhotra
description: Design and implement a preemptive 'soft-fallback' controller that proactively routes requests away from stressed regions/tiers or to cheaper/faster model variants before hard failures occur. Provide rich decision telemetry so SREs/PMs can understand why a fallback decision was taken (signals, scoring, hysteresis). This is intended to reduce visible 429s/timeouts and improve graceful degradation while preserving explainability for rollouts and incident postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can subscribe to existing routing signals (429 rate, 95/99th tail latency, in-flight queue length, backend error-rate) and compute a numeric risk score per region-tier-tenant
Fallback decisions are executed as 'soft' reroutes (percent-based redirect) rather than immediate hard cutovers, with configurable hysteresis and probation windows
Every decision emits a structured telemetry event (decision_id, signals_at_decision, chosen_action, previous_state, decay_ttl, related_request_examples) surfaced in Console Decision Log
Integration tests show a >= 35% reduction in end-user 429s during injected overload scenarios vs baseline routing with only reactive circuit breakers
No customer-facing SLA regressions in steady-state (10k QPS synthetic workload) for top 10 customers during staged rollout
Feature flag + kill switch available for emergency disable; RBAC control for manual overrides in Console
technical_notes: Risk scoring: linear combination of normalized signals with per-tenant weighting. Signals: recent_429_rate (window 1m/5m), tail_latency_95/99, request_queue_ratio, model_error_rate, cpu/gpu_utilization. Tunable coefficients stored in ConfigDB.
Action types: (a) percent_soft_reroute_to_region_variant, (b) route_to_lower_precision_model_variant, (c) throttle-nudge (soft 429s upstream) for low-priority routes.

Hysteresis: use two thresholds (warn, tripping). On crossing tripping threshold trigger soft-reroute; only escalate to hard circuit-breaker after configurable number of tripping events within decay window.
Probation: after a fallback, probation window begins where traffic is slowly ramped back (half-life decay) if signals improve. We track per-tenant probation score to avoid flip-flopping.

Telemetry: decision events use existing tracing header (x-rw-decision-id) and are emitted to Trace + Console Decision Log + metrics (prometheus counter + histogram of scores). Archived to long-term logging for postmortems.
Compatibility: falls back to existing circuit-breaker primitives; controller emits recommended actions which the router enforces so older routers can ignore telemetry until upgraded.

Scaling: stateless controller that reads compact counters from fast time-series (ringbuffer or cache) and writes actions to a central routing-config stream (Kafka). Ensure idempotency in action application.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives cause unnecessary cost (routing to larger/paid regions). Mitigation: conservative default coefficients, experiment with simulated load and a/b tests, billing alerting during rollout.
Risk: added routing churn (flip-flop). Mitigation: hysteresis + probation + minimum hold time for decisions; backoff multiplier on oscillating tenants.
Risk: telemetry volume and PII leakage. Mitigation: redact request payloads in decision events, sample high-volume tenants, and compress signals into aggregate buckets.
Risk: decision logic complexity makes debugging hard. Mitigation: decision_id + full signals snapshot saved to long-term storage; developer tool to replay decision with recorded signals.
Risk: performance overhead on router. Mitigation: controller emits sparse updates; router caches last-action and applies delta; only high-QPS tenants evaluated at higher cadence.
